title: Scalar extension of a prime-degree Galois field
statement: Let $p$ be prime, let $E/F$ be a finite Galois extension of fields of degree $p$, and let $F\to L$ be any field extension [def-pc-field-extension], [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Galois means separable and normal, with normal meaning that every irreducible polynomial over $F$ having a root in $E$ splits in $E$. Then the $L$-algebra $E\otimes_F L$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] is reduced and is either a field which is Galois of degree $p$ over $L$, or is isomorphic as an $L$-algebra to $\prod_{i=1}^p L$. Here reduced means that the only nilpotent element is zero; the field alternative has its canonical scalar map from $L$.

source.place: Tag 09F4, lemma-make-finite-level, proof second paragraph: split or degree-p field alternative under scalar extension. This is the general field-algebra fact used there, independent of DVR or finite-level hypotheses.

proof.text: Put $U=L\otimes_F E$, with $(l\otimes e)(l^{\prime}\otimes e^{\prime})=ll^{\prime}\otimes ee^{\prime}$ and scalar map $l\mapsto l\otimes1$. The swap $e\otimes l\mapsto l\otimes e$ is an $L$-algebra isomorphism from the algebra in the statement to $U$: its inverse is the same swap, and both preserve products of pure tensors. By [lem-pc-finrank-field-base-change], $\dim_LU=p$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-tensor-field-reduced], applied to $E/F$ and $L/F$ and then the swap, $U$ is reduced. In particular $U\ne0$, since $p>0$.

source.place: Tag 09F4, implicit scalar-algebra input; Algebra Tag 030U (lemma-separable-extension-preserves-reducedness); finite-dimensional scalar extension.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dim-algebra-artinian], $U$ is Artinian. Apply [lem-sfb-reduced-artinian-residue-product]: if $\mathcal M$ is its finite set of maximal ideals, the quotient map gives an $L$-algebra isomorphism $U\simeq\prod_{\mathfrak m\in\mathcal M}K_{\mathfrak m}$, with $K_{\mathfrak m}=U/\mathfrak m$ a field. Its $U$-algebra structure in the cited statement restricts to the specified $L$-algebra structure. Since $U\ne0$, this product is nonzero, so $r=|\mathcal M|>0$. Each $K_{\mathfrak m}$ is finite-dimensional over $L$: the images of any finite $L$-basis of $U$ span the quotient.

For $\mathfrak m,\mathfrak n\in\mathcal M$, both contract to zero in $L$: the scalar map into either quotient is a unital homomorphism between fields and hence injective. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-galois-prime-transitivity] with $k=F$, $K=E$, $A=L$. It gives $\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}_F(E)$ such that $T^{-1}(\mathfrak m)=\mathfrak n$, where $T(l\otimes e)=l\otimes\sigma(e)$. This formula is $F$-balanced and preserves multiplication, and the formula with $\sigma^{-1}$ gives its inverse. It fixes $L$. Therefore $[u]_{\mathfrak n}\mapsto[T(u)]_{\mathfrak m}$ and its inverse induce an $L$-algebra isomorphism $K_{\mathfrak n}\simeq K_{\mathfrak m}$. All these fields consequently have the same positive degree $d$ over $L$.

source.place: Varieties Tag 038B (lemma-closed-fixed-by-Galois), Galois invariants and prime transitivity; explicit quotient transport.

proof.text: Choose an $L$-basis of each $K_{\mathfrak m}$. In the finite product, the vectors with one basis element in one coordinate and zero elsewhere form a basis: coordinatewise expansion proves spanning, and projecting a relation to each coordinate proves independence. Thus step 2 gives $p=\dim_LU=rd$. Since $p$ is prime and $r,d>0$, either $r=1,d=p$ or $r=p,d=1$.

source.place: Tag 09F4, implicit prime-degree dichotomy; elementary basis and prime-divisor argument written by Q123.

proof.text: If $r=1$, step 2 identifies $U$ as an $L$-algebra with its unique field quotient $K$. It has degree $p$ by step 4. The maps $E\to K$, $e\mapsto[1\otimes e]$, and $L\to K$, $l\mapsto[l\otimes1]$, are unital field maps, so identify $E,L$ with their images. These images have compositum $K$: every element of $K$ is a finite sum of images of pure tensors, and $[l\otimes e]=[l\otimes1][1\otimes e]$, so belongs to that compositum. The image of $E$ is finite Galois over the common image of $F$. Apply [lem-sfb-galois-compositum-restriction] to these subfields of $K$ to obtain that $K/L$ is Galois. Hence $E\otimes_FL$ is a degree-$p$ Galois field with its canonical $L$-structure.

source.place: Tag 09F4, field alternative; Fields Galois compositum argument, as stated by IsGalois.sup_right in Mathlib/FieldTheory/Galois/Basic.lean:557.

proof.text: If $r=p,d=1$, the canonical scalar map $L\to K_{\mathfrak m}$ is an isomorphism for every $\mathfrak m$: it is injective, and $1\ne0$ is a basis of the one-dimensional $L$-vector space $K_{\mathfrak m}$, so the map is surjective. These are $L$-algebra isomorphisms. Enumerate the $p$ maximal ideals and take their product in step 2 to obtain $U\simeq L^p$ as $L$-algebras. Compose with the swap in step 1. Reducedness was already proved in step 1, so both alternatives and the reducedness clause follow.

source.place: Tag 09F4, split alternative; elementary one-dimensional field and product identification written by Q123.
